title: Replacing the Faucet Diverter Valve to Restore a Kitchen Sink Spray Hose
summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing a clogged faucet diverter for a kitchen sink spray hose and replacing the diverter assembly. After noting that the spray hose was not delivering water, the presenters turn off the water at under-sink shut-off valves, protect the chrome with a rag, and remove the cap to expose the diverter. They identify the diverter and its internal flapper, confirm a clog, and replace the diverter valve plus a gasket. The new unit arrives with pre-applied Teflon on the threads. After reassembling and tightening, they reopen the water and test the spray to verify the repair.

sections.title: Problem identification and faucet anatomy
sections.description: Identify the spray hose issue, discuss the faucet anatomy, and describe the paths of hot and cold supply lines before accessing the diverter.

sections.title: Access, protect, and remove the diverter cap
sections.description: Turn off the water, protect chrome with a rag, loosen the diverter cap with channel-lock pliers, and expose the diverter valve for inspection.

sections.title: Diverter replacement and system test
sections.description: Inspect the diverter internals for a clog, replace with a new diverter and gasket, note pre-applied Teflon on the new unit, reassemble, reopen water, and test the spray function.

featured_techniques.technique: Shut off water supply at under-sink valves (hot and cold)
Protect chrome with rag and loosen cap
Remove and inspect the diverter valve (identify internal flapper)
Install new diverter with gasket and pre-applied Teflon
